A linear program

Real variables, a maximised objective, three constraints: a bakery with flour, butter and oven time. check reads the model and says what kind it is; run solves it and re-checks its own answer (verified).

// A bakery has 40 kg of flour, 8 kg of butter and 10 oven hours today.
// Per batch: a loaf needs 2 kg flour, 0.5 kg butter, 1 oven hour and sells for 12;
// a tray of croissants needs 1 kg flour, 1.5 kg butter, 0.5 oven hour and sells for 18.
// A batch can be fractional (half a tray is fine), so this is a linear program.
var loaf   : real 0..20;
var tray   : real 0..20;

maximize sales: 12*loaf + 18*tray;

subject to
    flour:  2*loaf + 1*tray   <= 40;
    butter: 0.5*loaf + 1.5*tray <= 8;
    oven:   1*loaf + 0.5*tray <= 10;
check and run
$ solve check < bakery.sol
{"status":"ok","class":"LP","variables":2,"integer":0,"constraints":3,"nonzeros":6,"objective":"maximize"}
$ solve run < bakery.sol
{"status":"optimal","objective":148.8,"x":{"loaf":8.8,"tray":2.4},"verified":true,"max_violation":0.0,"stats":{"iterations":2,"rows":3,"columns":2}}

iterations is the number of simplex pivots; max_violation is the largest constraint violation of the printed point, computed by the printer.

A mixed-integer program

bool and int variables make it a MIP: run branches. stats.nodes counts the LPs solved; bound is the best value the search can still not rule out. --relax drops integrality and solves the LP relaxation, whose value is the upper bound of a maximisation.

// A courier van carries at most 15 kg. Six parcels, each taken whole or left behind:
// weight in kg, and the fee the courier earns for delivering it.
param n   = 6;
param w   = [12, 2, 1, 4, 7, 5];
param fee = [4, 2, 1, 10, 8, 6];
param cap = 15;

var take[0..n] : bool;

maximize income: sum i in 0..n: fee[i] * take[i];

subject to
    weight: sum i in 0..n: w[i] * take[i] <= cap;
run and run --relax
$ solve run < van.sol
{"status":"optimal","objective":21.0,"bound":21.0,"x":{"take[0]":0.0,"take[1]":1.0,"take[2]":1.0,"take[3]":1.0,"take[4]":1.0,"take[5]":0.0},"verified":true,"max_violation":0.0,"stats":{"iterations":6,"rows":1,"columns":6,"nodes":7,"branched":4,"method":"dense"}}
$ solve run --relax < van.sol
{"status":"optimal","relaxed":true,"objective":22.857142857142858,"x":{"take[0]":0.0,"take[1]":0.0,"take[2]":0.0,"take[3]":1.0,"take[4]":0.8571428571428572,"take[5]":1.0},"verified":true,"max_violation":0.0,"stats":{"iterations":1,"rows":1,"columns":6}}

The relaxation takes fractional parcels (fee 22.857142857142858 against 21.0 whole parcels), which is why the search has to branch.

The flat model

expand prints what a solver reads: every variable with its bounds, the objective and every constraint, with the sums and loops written out. It is the model the checker and the verifier both stand on.

expand
$ solve expand < van.sol
{"variables":[{"name":"take[0]","kind":"bool","lo":0.0,"hi":1.0},{"name":"take[1]","kind":"bool","lo":0.0,"hi":1.0},"\u2026"],"objective":{"sense":"maximize","name":"income","constant":0.0,"terms":[[0,4.0],[1,2.0],[2,1.0],[3,10.0],[4,8.0],[5,6.0]]},"constraints":[{"name":"weight","sense":"<=","rhs":15.0,"terms":[[0,12.0],[1,2.0],[2,1.0],[3,4.0],[4,7.0],[5,5.0]]}]}

Two of the six variables shown; the rest are the same shape.

Stopping early

A limit stops the search and says so: the status is unknown or feasible, with a bound (and gap, when there is an incumbent), and the exit status is 1. A limit never prints a wrong optimum.

node and iteration limits
$ solve run --node-limit 3 < van.sol
{"status":"unknown","limit":"nodes","bound":22.857142857142858,"stats":{"iterations":3,"rows":1,"columns":6,"nodes":3,"branched":3,"method":"dense"}}
# exit status 1
$ solve run --iteration-limit 1 < bakery.sol
{"status":"unknown","limit":"iterations","stats":{"iterations":1,"rows":3,"columns":2}}
# exit status 1

Dense and sparse

--method dense|sparse|auto picks the LP engine; auto (the default) takes the sparse one when the matrix is at most 4% full or the tableau would not fit. Both print the same optimum; the stats differ.

--method
$ solve run --method dense < bakery.sol
{"status":"optimal","objective":148.8,"x":{"loaf":8.8,"tray":2.4},"verified":true,"max_violation":0.0,"stats":{"iterations":2,"rows":3,"columns":2}}
$ solve run --method sparse < bakery.sol
{"status":"optimal","objective":148.8,"x":{"loaf":8.8,"tray":2.4},"verified":true,"max_violation":0.0,"stats":{"iterations":2,"rows":3,"columns":2,"refactorisations":2}}

A second opinion

solve verify takes a model and a claimed solution from any source and says whether it is feasible and has the objective it claims. A failure is a refusal: exit 2, a tag, and the violations. It does not prove optimality.

verify
# the model, a line holding exactly ---, then the claimed solution as JSON
$ (cat van.sol; echo ---; solve run < van.sol) | solve verify
{"status":"verified","objective":21.0,"objective_checked":true,"tolerance":0.000001,"max_bound_violation":0.0,"max_integrality_violation":0.0,"max_row_violation":0.0,"variables":6,"rows":1,"proves":"feasibility and the objective value, not optimality"}
# a claim that overloads the van: the row `weight` does not hold
$ (cat van.sol; echo ---; <take[0] set to 1>) | solve verify
{"error":"solve.row-violated","message":"a constraint does not hold at the claimed values","repair":"the solution is infeasible; solve again","count":2,"violations":[{"rule":"solve.row-violated","what":"weight","value":11.0,"limit":0.000027},{"rule":"solve.objective-mismatch","what":"objective","value":4.0,"limit":0.000026}]}
# exit status 2
# a claim whose objective is not the one its values give
$ (cat van.sol; echo ---; <objective set to 25>) | solve verify
{"error":"solve.objective-mismatch","message":"the claimed objective is not the objective evaluated at the claimed values","repair":"claim the evaluated objective, or drop the objective member","count":1,"violations":[{"rule":"solve.objective-mismatch","what":"objective","value":4.0,"limit":0.000022}]}
# exit status 2
# a half parcel in a bool variable
$ (cat van.sol; echo ---; <take[1] set to 0.5>) | solve verify
{"error":"solve.not-integral","message":"a bool or int variable has a fractional claimed value","repair":"round the value, or solve again","count":2,"violations":[{"rule":"solve.not-integral","what":"take[1]","value":0.5,"limit":0.000001},{"rule":"solve.objective-mismatch","what":"objective","value":1.0,"limit":0.000021}]}
# exit status 2

The tolerance is 1e-6 by default and is printed (--tolerance T). The verifier shares no code with the search (design.md section 20.1); what it shares is the parser and expander, because the claim is about that model.

Refusals are data

Every refusal is one JSON object on standard error with error (a stable tag), message, repair and, for a model, the position at. The exit status is 2. A model that is merely impossible is not a refusal: it is an answer, infeasible.

// A variable with no bounds: the checker refuses it before any solver sees it.
var x : real;
maximize x;
subject to c: x <= 4;
a variable with no bounds
$ solve check < unbounded.sol
{"error":"solve.unbounded-domain","message":"a variable has no bounds","repair":"write the bounds: var x : real 0..10;","at":{"line":2,"col":5}}
# exit status 2
// Two parcels that cannot both be taken and must both be taken.
var a : bool;
var b : bool;
maximize a + b;
subject to
    both:   a + b >= 2;
    either: a + b <= 1;
an impossible model is an answer
$ solve run < cannot.sol
{"status":"infeasible","stats":{"iterations":1,"rows":2,"columns":2,"nodes":1,"branched":0,"method":"dense"}}
an empty range, and a flag that does not exist
$ echo 'var x : int 5..2; minimize x;' | solve check
{"error":"solve.bad-bounds","message":"a bound is above the other, or an integer variable has a bound that is not whole","repair":"swap the bounds, or write whole numbers for an int variable","at":{"line":1,"col":9}}
# exit status 2
$ solve run --bogus
{"error":"solve.usage","message":"usage: solve check | expand | run [--relax] [--iteration-limit N] [--method dense|sparse|auto] [--node-limit N] [--node-select depth|best] [--branching fractional|pseudo] | verify [--tolerance T] | introspect | skill","repair":"pass one verb; check, expand, run and verify read the model on standard input"}
# exit status 2
cancho-solveEUPL-1.2written in cancho RepositoryDesignFor agents
